Bow.name: Bow
Bow.description: Bow pose can be thought of as a reverse bridge. This position is more challenging than bridge however, even though it utilises the same areas of flexibility in the hip flexors, shoulders and back. With bow pose there is a large element of strength involved. Strength from the hip flexors to extend and drive the legs upwards, and strength needed from the shoulders to extend up the away from the body to create the teardrop shape.

Bow.name: Bow with single foot on shoulder
Bow with both feet on shoulders
Bow.description: Holding ankles and arching back in backbend while bringing the feet to the tops of the shoulders

Bow.name: Bow with straight legs
Bow.description: Holding ankles and arching back in backbend while extending legs upwards until straight

Bow.name: Bow with headsit and straight legs
Bow.description: Holding ankles and arching back in backbend while extending legs upwards until straight and resting the back of the head against the glutes

Box split.name: Frog
Box split.description: Frog is one of the great first stages of working towards box splits. The full expression of frog pose is quite challenging, requiring lots of flexibility in the adductors to get the complete inside of both thighs flush with the floor. This pose is ideal for progressions and allows the performer to easily see progress.

Box split.name: Pancake
Box split.description: Pancake is an important foundation pose that enables other poses such as fold through.

Box split.name: Box split
Box split.description: Box split is one of the great "big three" contortion poses that beginners should without question look to master. It has great use both on the floor and in the air as a trick as well as helping to unlock more advanced hip-based poses.

Bridge.name: Glute bridge
Bridge.description: Glute bridge could be seen as one of the very first forays into backbending that puts much more emphasis on using the glutes (as the name suggests) rather than loading anything into the back or shoulders as would be required for other poses. This foundation exercise is best paired with some of the other foundation or beginner backbending poses to help build up overall capability towards the bridge pose

Bridge.name: Raised bridge (Feet raised)
Bridge.description: Raised bridge provides a more accessible version of bridge pose.

Bridge.name: Bridge with straight legs with feet away from hands
Bridge.description: This is a good variation of bridge to train alongside regular bridge. For most training bridge with straight legs is actually more beneficial as it allows contortion practitioners to access more of their upper back and shoulder flexibility. Moving the load to this area means that it is less likely to impact the lower back which can cause discomfort.

Bridge.name: Bridge
Bridge.description: There are many ways to enter the bridge pose. The most common method is to enter for laying on the floor with knees bent, feet placed close to the glutes. The hands on on the floor, fingers pointing towards your toes, underneath your shoulders. From here you then push up into bridge, locking out your arms and pushing into your shoulders so that your arms are perpendicular to the floor. The bridge pose is one of the foundation poses in contortionist training. It is a backbend that utilises large movements in the hip flexors and the shoulders, making it a very useful pose to help progress other areas of a contortionist’s overall backbending ability. The bridge pose is also a very good beginning pose as it easily modified to make way for progressions. From the bridge you can progress to have feet and ankles get closer and from there grabbing the ankles. Another variation is a Gymnastic Bridge whereby you push largely into the shoulders and keep the legs locked out, and straight. In yoga the bridge gets called “wheel” or Chakrasana. More colloquially and in other disciplines this pose gets called “crab”.

Bridge.name: Bridge with straight legs leaning into shoulders
Bridge stagged with bent leg
Bridge.description: This pose is a subtle variation of the straight legged bridge. Instead of both legs out straight, one is brought in to change the shape of the pose. This can be the beginning pose of a transition to a stagged contortion handstand.

Bridge.name: Bridge on elbows
Bridge.description: A variation of the regular bridge is to do it with straight legs which puts more emphasis on using the upper back and shoulders. This works in a similar way to

Bridge.name: Bridge stagged with bent raised leg
Bridge.description: This is fairly simple alternative variation to bridge pose. The contortionist raises one leg off the floor, bends the knee fully and points their toes. This can be incorporated into other transitions such as walkovers

Bridge.name: Bridge with straight legs feet by hands
Bridge.description: This is a slightly more advanced version of the regular bridge as it requires more spinal flexion in order to get the hands and feet to meet. This is a likely good precursor to the bridge ankle catch but also for much more advanced tricks like bridge with ankle catch and backfold.

Bridge.name: Bridge chair-sit
Bridge.description: A variation of bridge pose which is completed by driving the hips and glutes downwards towards the floor while keeping pushed into the shoulders. This ensures that the upper back is engaged as much as possible. In the final version of this pose the contortionist would bring their glutes to rest on top of the head.

Bridge.name: Bridge on elbows holding ankles
Bridge.description: This variation of bridge is a good way to prepare for the more advanced ankle catch bridge, but also allows to work different areas of flexibility such as in the shoulders while the arms are bent. This is also a potential starting entry point to move into a chest stand face frame if you are at that level.

Bridge.name: Bridge ankle catch
Bridge.description: This is the final progression of bridge pose whereby the contortionist takes their hands off the floor and grasps their ankles, knees or upper leg and brings their head towards their glutes. Completion of this advanced pose requires advanced shoulder as well as hip flexor flexibility. It can be entered in various different ways. Some prefer to start from the floor and walk their hands in towards their legs. Other contortionists prefer to hang back into the pose and then grab each leg or ankle individually without touching the floor.

Bridge.name: Bridge on elbows face cradle headsit
Bridge with arms around thighs and bent legs
Bridge with backfold hands in front of feet
Bridge with arms around thighs and straight legs

Butterfly.name: Butterfly
Butterfly.description: Butterfly pose is a foundation pose that stretches the groin and less so, the hamstrings, depending on how far your feet are away from you. To enter the pose, sit with back straight legs outstretched. You then bend your knees and bring your feet together and towards your body in one movement, sometimes it helps to guide your feet while cupping them with your hands. The deal progression for this pose to to have your knee flush with the floor and the feet only a few centimetres away from your groin.

Chest stand.name: Chest stand
Chest stand.description: Chest stand is probably one of the most sought after poses in contortion and is considered a milestone when it is reached. The position itself looks like an impressive and impossible feature of flexibility. It combines flexibility in many different areas such as the back, hips shoulders and neck. Chest stand can be modified in many ways and opens up the possibilities for several different advanced versions once the basic chest stand in mastered.

Chest stand.name: Chest stand with bent legs and arms crossed over feet chin on floor
Chest stand.description: Most often referred to as chest stand face frame, this pose is usually the next variation that performers will look at working towards once they have a comfortable grasp on their basic chest stand. In this pose the performer wraps their arms around their ankles while hugging their feet towards their shoulders. This also sets up for the more advanced variation where the performer will lift their chin off the floor and look at their audience, and in very advanced cases transition into the backfold pose while the head lifted between the knees.

Chest stand with straight legs arms forward
Chest stand with straight legs feet on floor
Chest stand headsit with straight legs  and feet on floor
Chest stand.description: One of the most common variations of chest stand headsit is where the performer has their legs locked out straight with their feet on the floor. From this position it allows different combinations of arm positions, such as lifting the arms from the floor. This pose is usually one of the first precursory steps to working towards the Marinelli trick.

Cobra.name: Cobra
Cobra.description: Cobra pose is a foundation backbending pose. This pose stretches the abdominals and the lower and thoracic spine

Cobra.name: Cobra head to feet
Cobra.description: This is the next progression of cobra once you have mastered the foundation cobra pose. This version of cobra is completed by bending your knees and bringing your feet to rest on the crown of your head. This utilises your hip flexors as well as multiple areas of your back. It also requires some hamstring strength to bring your feet to your head while the back is arched.

Pike.name: Pike while standing
Pike.description: Pike pose while standing helps with developing your hamstring flexibility.

Pike.name: Pike
Pike.description: Pike pose is one of the fundamental foundation poses when you're starting off in your contortion training.

Pike.name: Fold through
Pike.description: Fold through is a classic frontbending pose that is a great progression for those working towards human knot after attaining tricks such as pike or pancake. Fold through utilises a performer's hamstring flexibility as well as quad strength. This trick also makes use of back flexibility. Good form of this pose is to have straight legs with the head moving away from the glutes, trying to use as little back arch as possible.

Front split.name: Lunge
Front split.description: The most simple pose of the lunge sequence. Training pre-requisite for front splits and backbends.

Human Knot.name: Human Knot
Human Knot.description: Human knot is one of the classic staples of a frontbending performance. This pose is completed by the performer placing both feet behind their neck, crossed at the ankles. The best form for this trick is through keeping the back as flat as possible with the hips doing as much of the work as they will allow. The most basic variety of this pose is performing it laying down, doing it this way means that a performer doesn't have to worry about finding their balance as they are placing their feet.

Human Knot.name: Human Knot armbalance
Human Knot.description: When a performer is able to put their feet behind their head in an upright position this then allows for the transition onto their hands by lifting their body off the ground. Having a flat back in this pose makes lifting off the ground easier and makes it less likely that you will fall forwards.

Human knot with ankles under opposite arms
Human Knot.description: More commonly called DeMario pose, this is the pinnacle pose of the leg behind head series of poses (that the vast majority of people that train for it can attain). This pose is extreme in the position that it puts the contortionist in, and even more extreme in the technique needed to get into the pose alone and with the right amount if finessé that would be required on stage.

Human knot with ankles under opposite arms on front with arms over legs while upright

Kandasana.name: Kandasana armbalance
Kandasana.description: One of the easier next progressions for kandasana is to elevate the body so that the knees come off the floor.

Kneeling backbend.name: Kneeling backbend
Kneeling backbend.description: This is one of the first progressions towards very advanced poses such as triple fold.

Kneeling backbend.name: Kneeling backbend ankle catch
Kneeling backbend.description: Kneeling backbends are an interesting variation to backbending sequences.

Kneeling backbend.name: Kneeling backbend with knee catch
Kneeling backbend.description: Once a contortionist is more comfortable with grabbing their ankles, they will eventually reach their knees.

Leg behind back.description: This pose is also known as leg under armpit pose and is the natural progression of a contortionist furthering their leg behind head practice.

Leg behind head.description: The next progression of lunge is to lower to the floor with a flat back.

Leg behind head.name: Pidgeon
Leg behind head.description: Pigeon pose is another great foundation pose. This position is the precursor to much of the leg behind head sequence.

Leg behind head.name: Squat
Leg behind head.description: Squat is a fundamental pose for many hip-related poses.
